passage:
A museum recreated a classroom from a century ago. There were wooden desks, ink bottles, strict rules on the wall, and a blackboard.
Students sat inside and tried writing with old pens. It was slow and messy.
The guide asked them what had changed and what had not. Tools had changed. Subjects had changed. But students still worried about mistakes, teachers still explained ideas, and classrooms still shaped habits.
The old classroom felt both strange and familiar.
Education is never only about books. It is also about furniture, rules, technology, and what society expects children to become.
